item.title: Situational Awareness Not Target of Predatory Shorts, S3 Says
item.description: The losses that forced hedge fund Situational Awareness to sell stocks at deep discounts appear to be the result of highly concentrated positions in crowded trades, rather than a concerted effort by short-sellers, according to the founder of a company that analyzes short positioning data.

item.title: AMD Sales Outlook Disappoints Investors After AI-Fueled Rally
item.description: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. disappointed investors with its latest sales outlook, a sign shareholders expected more of a return from the global expansion of AI data centers.

item.title: Pinterest Revenue Outlook Disappoints Investors; Shares Slide
item.description: Pinterest Inc. gave a revenue outlook for the current quarter that disappointed investors worried about the company’s momentum despite posting strong user and revenue growth for the prior period.

item.title: Tanger Sees Boost from World Cup, Back to School Shoppers
item.description: Tanger Inc. boosted its outlook for a second time this year, as stronger domestic travel and early back-to-school shoppers have boosted traffic and sales at the real estate investment trust’s shopping centers.

item.title: Match’s Quarterly Revenue, Outlook Fall Shy of Analyst Estimates
item.description: Match Group Inc. gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that narrowly missed analysts’ estimates, suggesting its dating sites still need to attract more younger users as part of its turnaround effort.

item.title: USD And JPY: Trump, Bessent Intervene to Rescue a Weakening Japanese Yen
item.description: One of the most dramatic foreign exchange market interventions in decades aims to stabilize the slumping yen — and stave off a larger crisis.

item.title: EchoStar’s Hughes Wins Approval to Use Lender Cash in Bankruptcy
item.description: A judge has allowed Hughes Satellite Systems Corp. to use noteholders’ cash to keep operating for the next four weeks, after a two-day court fight over how the company will pay its bills while in bankruptcy.

item.title: Cerberus Seeks $4 Billion for Second Supply Chain Fund
item.description: Cerberus Capital Management, co-founded by Deputy Secretary of Defense Stephen Feinberg, is looking to raise at least $4 billion for its latest supply-chain fund that backs investments critical to the US economy.

item.title: Samsung Reveals New 3D-Memory Roadmap in Bid for AI Tech Lead
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. offered a glimpse of its most advanced memory hardware, touting improved performance and power efficiency in a bid to overtake rivals SK Hynix Inc. and Micron Technology Inc. in the race for long-term dominance.

item.title: Thousands Seek NYC Pied-a-Terre Tax Relief, City Hall Says
item.description: Roughly 2,000 people have completed applications seeking an exemption from New York City’s newly-implemented pied-à-terre tax, a spokesperson for the Department of Finance said Tuesday.

item.title: Data Centers Exposed US Telecoms to China Hacks, US Panel to Say
item.description: US telecommunications companies connected their systems to data centers and related infrastructure in a way that exposed them to cybersecurity vulnerabilities, potentially opening the door to the massive Salt Typhoon hacking campaign that breached several mobile carriers two years ago, according to an upcoming House committee’s report.

item.title: Palantir Short Sellers Take $3 Billion Hit After 30% Stock Surge
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc.’s stock surge has wiped out all of the year-to-date paper gains for short sellers, saddling them with billions in losses.

item.title: AI’s Great Reverse Run On The Bank
item.description: When people run towards the source of panic.

item.title: AI Boom Is ‘Trickling Down’ to Old-Line Stocks, Wells Fargo Says
item.description: The flood of AI spending by big tech companies is “trickling down to the broader economy,” according to Wells Fargo & Co., which says that’s poised to push up industrial stocks.

item.title: Italy Extends Diesel Tax Cut Through Aug. 25, La Stampa Reports
item.description: Italy’s cabinet extended a cut in diesel taxes through Aug. 25, La Stampa reported.

item.title: Thoma Bravo Sells Majority Stake in Command Alkon to Francisco Partners
item.description: Buyout firm Francisco Partners has agreed to acquire a majority stake in construction software maker Command Alkon Inc. from Thoma Bravo, underscoring investor interest in software crucial to specific industries.

item.title: Codelco Halts Expansion Project at Top Mine on New Seismic Risk
item.description: Codelco is suspending work on a project designed to extend the life of its biggest copper mine after identifying a new source of seismic risk a year after a rock burst killed six workers.

item.title: Jefferies Gets New Evidence of Fake Invoices at Beleaguered Fund
item.description: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. has been told that some of the invoices underpinning its financing to an iron ore trader called Sapphire Minmetals Corp. are not genuine, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: OPEC Output Rose in July Led by Gulf Nations, Survey Shows
item.description: OPEC’s crude oil production recouped some more of its wartime losses last month with gains in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Iraq, though opaque shipping data complicated the process of tracking the group’s output, a Bloomberg survey showed.

item.title: SpaceX Earnings Live: SPCX First Public Results, Elon Musk Comments
item.description: SpaceX Earnings Live: SPCX First Public Results, Elon Musk Comments【原文：SpaceX Earnings Live: SPCX First Public Results, Elon Musk Comments】

item.title: Griffin’s NYC Office Tower Set to Land $3.3 Billion Construction Loan
item.description: The team working on Citadel’s new Manhattan skyscraper expects to secure a $3.3 billion construction loan for the project.

item.title: Apple Gears Up for September iPhone Launch With Retail Employee Lottery
item.description: With Apple Inc. gearing up for its biggest product launch of the year, the company is opening a lottery for US retail employees who want to help staff the in-person unveiling.

item.title: Novo Nordisk Boosts Forecast on Soaring GLP-1 Sales
item.description: Novo Nordisk A/S raised its forecast for the second time this year, citing higher expectations for its obesity and diabetes drug sales.

item.title: Hellman & Friedman’s Baker Tilly Calls Off $3 Billion Debt Deal
item.description: Baker Tilly has dropped plans for a roughly $3 billion leveraged loan that was intended to refinance private credit debt and fund a dividend, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Madagascar Hikes Rate for First Time in Over a Year on War Risks
item.description: Madagascar joined a handful of central banks in raising interest rates after revising its inflation forecasts higher as renewed tensions between the US and Iran stoke price pressures.

item.title: T-Mobile Adds Financing for New Phone Fees to Sweeten Upgrades
item.description: T-Mobile US Inc. will allow customers to finance taxes and fees associated with their new handsets in addition to the cost of the device, letting users take home a new phone with no money down. The initiative, announced Tuesday, comes as customers are keeping handsets longer and the industry is shifting away from providing device subsidies.

item.title: Apple Asks Judge to Bar OpenAI From Using Alleged Trade Secrets
item.description: Apple Inc. asked a federal judge to immediately order OpenAI to stop using what it calls stolen trade secrets, the latest salvo in its lawsuit accusing the artificial intelligence company of engaging in a coordinated campaign to steal proprietary information about upcoming products.

item.title: AI Now Fuels Over Half of Africa’s Cybercrime, Study Finds
item.description: Artificial intelligence is fueling more than half of cybercrime in Africa, enabling criminals to launch faster, more sophisticated attacks as financial losses continue to mount, a new study found.

item.title: OpenAI Settles Worker Discrimination Allegations With DOJ
item.description: A unit of OpenAI has reached a settlement with the US Justice Department to resolve allegations that the California-based artificial intelligence company discriminated against US workers.

item.title: South Africa Seeks Advisers for Creditor Talks on Eskom Spin Off
item.description: South Africa will hire advisers in the coming weeks to begin negotiations with lenders on a plan to spin off state-owned power utility Eskom Holdings SOC Ltd.’s transmission subsidiary, according to the head of the National Treasury.
